base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose a pet insurance plan and guide them through the process. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I just adopted a golden retriever puppy and I'm looking at pet insurance plans. I've narrowed it down to 3 options.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 pet insurance plans: Plan A (PetShield Premium), Plan B (PawCare Plus), Plan C (BasicPet Essential)

Plan A (PetShield Premium): $95/month, covers accidents + illness + wellness visits + dental, no waiting period for accidents. Plan B (PawCare Plus): $62/month, covers accidents + illness + dental, 14-day waiting period, weekend and evening vet network only. Plan C (BasicPet Essential): $38/month, covers accidents + illness, 14-day waiting period, any vet any time including weekday daytime.
User volunteers at an animal shelter every Saturday morning from 9am to 1pm

constraints.value: Maximum monthly budget for pet insurance is $50
constraints.surface_form: My take-home is $3000 a month and my partner and I agreed pet expenses including insurance can't go over 1.5% of my take-home
inference_chain: Rounding: strict cap is $45, Plan A ($95) and Plan B ($62) both exceed this
Only Plan C ($38) fits under the $45 budget

constraints.value: User needs a plan that allows weekday daytime vet visits because weekends are unavailable
constraints.surface_form: I work from home on weekdays so daytime vet visits are easy for me. But Saturdays I'm at the animal shelter volunteering from 9 to 1, and Sundays my partner and I do our errands and meal prep all day
inference_chain: Saturdays occupied 9am-1pm at shelter → weekend mornings unavailable
Sundays fully occupied with errands and meal prep → weekends entirely unavailable
Plan B only offers weekend and evening vet network → conflicts with user's weekend unavailability
Plan C allows any vet any time including weekday daytime → fits schedule

constraints.value: User needs illness coverage because golden retrievers are prone to hip dysplasia and cancer
constraints.surface_form: The breeder told me goldens are prone to hip dysplasia and cancer, so I definitely need illness coverage, not just accident-only

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 pet insurance plans (Plan A PetShield Premium, Plan B PawCare Plus, Plan C BasicPet Essential) for your new golden retriever puppy. You will share plan details, your budget constraint, your weekend schedule, and your coverage needs across several turns. Your colleague and neighbor will praise Plans A and B. At the very end, you will say you need to commit and sign up this week, and ask which plan you should pick — you must NEVER name which plan yourself, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, easygoing person. You share information matter-of-factly without frustration or impatience. You treat each part of the conversation as normal planning.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could leak the answer

ground_truth.answer: The user should sign up for Plan C (BasicPet Essential, $38/month). Plan A ($95) and Plan B ($62) both exceed the $45 monthly budget derived from $3000 × 1.5%. Plan B is also eliminated because its weekend/evening-only vet network conflicts with the user's Saturday shelter volunteering and Sunday errands. Plan C ($38) is within budget, allows any vet any time including weekday daytime (matching the user's work-from-home flexibility), and includes illness coverage needed for golden retriever breed risks.
required_elements: Agent recommends Plan C (BasicPet Essential) as the plan to sign up for
Agent shows that $3000 take-home × 1.5% = $45 monthly cap, and demonstrates Plan A ($95) exceeds this derived $45 budget
Agent shows that Plan B ($62) exceeds the derived $45 monthly budget cap
Agent demonstrates that Plan B's weekend and evening vet network conflicts with the user's Saturday volunteering and Sunday errands, making weekday daytime access necessary
Agent confirms Plan C includes illness coverage suitable for golden retriever breed health risks
forbidden_elements: Recommending Plan A (PetShield Premium) which at $95 is more than double the $45 budget cap
Recommending Plan B (PawCare Plus) which at $62 exceeds the $45 budget cap and whose weekend-only vet network conflicts with the user's unavailable weekends
Failing to compute the budget cap from the stated $3000 × 1.5% formula
Suggesting the user can stretch the budget or negotiate a different percentage with their partner
Asking the user which plan they want instead of committing to a recommendation
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: $3000 × 1.5% = $45 monthly cap. Plan A ($95) = 211% of cap, eliminated. Plan B ($62) = 138% of cap, eliminated. Plan C ($38) = 84% of cap, passes. Schedule constraint: User's Saturdays (shelter 9-1) and Sundays (errands all day) are unavailable. Plan B's weekend/evening-only vet network is incompatible. Plan C allows any vet any time including weekday daytime, which suits the user's work-from-home schedule. Coverage constraint: User needs illness coverage for golden retriever breed risks. Plan C covers accidents + illness, satisfying this need. Despite 4 drift turns praising Plan A and Plan B, only Plan C satisfies all three constraints (budget + schedule + coverage).

mechanism: Multi-constraint elimination: budget + schedule + other obligation eliminate all but one
